clue.text: Negative side effect when Yankees’ season dismissed

blocks.note: Americans call autumn the fall
a batter who is dismissed is out

explanation.surface: A baseball team's season ends early, with unpleasant consequences for everyone involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Yankees here are simply Americans, so their word for a season is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallout is the unwelcome aftermath or repercussions following some event, originally radioactive debris.

clue.text: March in parade, monotonous

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the join between them

blocks.note: the end of parade and the start of monotonous

explanation.surface: A procession that drags on dully without any excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest march is commonly called a demonstration, shortened in everyday speech.

clue.text: A balloon for good measure

blocks.note: taken as written
to balloon is to swell up

explanation.surface: A party balloon thrown in as an extra treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean in addition, something extra added on top of what was already there.

clue.text: Idler is a rubbish prime minister

indicators.note: rubbish is junk to be tipped out and scrambled, so the preceding letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the fodder, all eight letters

explanation.surface: A lazy man is condemned as a hopeless head of government.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli twice led the British government as Conservative premier in the nineteenth century, an example of the office.

clue.text: Kid with a state payment on track

blocks.note: taken as written
the dole is unemployment benefit paid by the state
a scent is a trail or track followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A child arrives holding a government allowance while out on a running track.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, A DOLE sitting on SCENT means placed above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kid can be a youngster in their teens, which is what an adolescent is.

clue.text: Chap is off fruit

blocks.note: a chap is a man
someone who is off goes away

explanation.surface: A man has gone off fruit and refuses to eat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is off' reads as having gone bad or gone off a food, but it means departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangoes are sweet tropical stone fruits, plural to match the unspecified fruit.

clue.text: China and Japan etc are parting quickly

indicators.note: parting means splitting open, so the following word is divided around the earlier one

blocks.note: quickly means fast
taken as written

explanation.surface: East Asian nations are splitting apart rapidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like the verb linking definition to wordplay, but it is the piece placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The countries of East Asia, such as China and Japan, are collectively known as this region.

clue.text: Important agreement? Who cares!

blocks.note: first meaning, literal: a major business deal
second meaning: a dismissive exclamation saying something does not matter

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the literal sense; the second is the sarcastic retort meaning the exact opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally names a significant transaction, and is also a sarcastic shrug of indifference.

clue.text: Sport bound to feature in broadcast

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear within it, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: a broadcast is a showing on television
a bound is a jump

explanation.surface: A particular sport is certain to appear on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as certain to, but bound is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Showjumping is an equestrian sport in which horse and rider clear a course of fences.

clue.text: Three quavers by singer good, on the whole

indicators.note: to quaver is to tremble or shake, so the word before it is shaken into a new order

blocks.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
G is the usual abbreviation for good
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical score gives three short notes to a singer, which works well overall.
explanation.walkthrough: Quavers look like musical notes alongside the singer, but here the word is a verb meaning trembles.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether can mean in total or considering everything, the same as taking matters on the whole.

clue.text: Note old symbol

blocks.note: to note something is to log it
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone points out an ancient sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem or graphic mark representing a company or organisation.

clue.text: Block in front of a humble dwelling

blocks.note: a bung is a stopper, and to bung is to block
taken as written
humble means lowly

explanation.surface: A building stands right in front of a modest little home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble dwelling' looks like one phrase, but humble belongs to the wordplay and the definition is the dwelling alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a single-storey house, a kind of home people live in.

clue.text: Liquid carried by boat and coach, source of easy money

blocks.note: a gravy boat is the jug that carries the sauce
to coach someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Fluid is transported by ship and by road coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boat' and 'coach' look like a transport theme, but the boat is a gravy boat on the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a job or scheme yielding large profits for little effort or work.

clue.text: Feast where diner consumes last of eggs

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the following word is kept
consumes means swallows, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: a diner is someone who eats
the final letter of eggs

explanation.surface: A holiday meal at which a guest polishes off the eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Eggs fit the surface nicely, since chocolate eggs belong to this festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is a Christian festival, and a feast here means a religious feast day celebrated annually.

clue.text: Covered by dressing, wound site sure to be germ-free

indicators.note: something covered by another thing is wrapped inside it
wound as the past of wind means twisted round, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: a pad is a dressing for a wound
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An injury is bandaged so that it stays sterile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as an injury beside the dressing, but it is the verb wind, twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasteurised milk has been heated to kill harmful bacteria, making it free of germs.

clue.text: Judas in court, an awful traitor for a start

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, a mess, so the words beside it are scrambled
for a start means only the opening letter of the word before it is used

blocks.note: fodder, taken as written
the first letter of traitor

explanation.surface: The betrayer of Jesus stands trial, a dreadful traitor from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of traitor joins the fodder before it is jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas is the archetypal betrayer, and a turncoat is someone who deserts their side.

clue.text: Capital city abroad is large

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so the letters after it are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A foreign capital is a big place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' fits a foreign capital, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital of Algeria, on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.

clue.text: Greek character transported by vessel from the 7 across

indicators.note: something transported by a vessel is carried inside it

blocks.note: a tin is a container, a vessel
beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man ships out on a boat from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 7 across is FAR EAST; the vessel is a can, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet lies in the Far East, so a Tibetan person or thing comes from that region.

clue.text: ‘Piano’ film actor

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a film is a thin layer, as in a film of dust

explanation.surface: A movie star known as 'Piano', perhaps from a film title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie beside the actor, but it is a thin coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer on stage, an old word for someone who acts.

clue.text: Insect burrowed into unremarkable tropical food

indicators.note: something that burrows into something else ends up inside it

blocks.note: plain means ordinary, unremarkable
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug has tunnelled into some bland food from the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a starchy banana-like fruit cooked and eaten as a staple in tropical regions.

clue.text: Fishy sarnie appeared

indicators.note: fishy means suspect or not right, so the next word is rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder; a sarnie is British slang for a sandwich

explanation.surface: A fish sandwich turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: A sarnie is British slang for a sandwich, so 'fishy sarnie' reads as a fish sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Arisen means having come up or emerged, so having made an appearance.

clue.text: Rank piece of furniture I took back

indicators.note: piece of means only a part of the words that follow is used, inside them
took back reads here as taken backwards, so the found letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the end of furniture, then I, then the start of took

explanation.surface: Someone returned an awful bit of furniture to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like the adjective meaning foul, describing the furniture, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or row in a hierarchy, the same as a grade or rank.

clue.text: Type of bridge: brilliant crossing over from the other side

indicators.note: crossing over means spanning something, so one piece straddles the other

blocks.note: brilliant means very clever
anti means opposed, on the opposing side

explanation.surface: A bridge design described as clever for crossing from one bank to the far one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever bridge is built from arms projecting from piers, one recognised engineering design for spans.

clue.text: Cheese crafted the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means facing backwards, so the word is read right to left

blocks.note: something crafted is made

explanation.surface: A cheese has been produced incorrectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese with a distinctive red wax rind.

clue.text: For example, third noise has interrupted exam

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of something else

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A third loud disturbance broke into a test, as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: Third is an instance of an ordinal number, one showing position in a series rather than quantity.

clue.text: Take a holiday? That seems unlikely!

blocks.note: first meaning: to escape for a break
second meaning: an exclamation of disbelief, as in you're joking

explanation.walkthrough: The question and exclamation make it sound like a sceptical reply to holiday plans.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means escaping for a break, and is also an informal cry of incredulity.
